rationale: Strong P1 case: the SHA-256-of-own-source mechanism literally enacts the tautology it names, and the re-hash loop proves the certificate void the instant it is issued — the infrathin twist is built into the execution, not bolted on. The double-coding is clean (an official-looking certificate vs. the literal collapse of authenticity into faithful copying), the four-beat footer ('No cookies. No trackers. No network. No blockchain.') lands the NFT jab without preachiness, and the live, per-visit, client-side nature makes it unprintable. The Judd/Flavin lineage and the Duchampian infrathin are correctly placed within the catalogue's ongoing argument about value, authenticity, and reproduction.
reservations: Materially distinct from The Original (2026) in mechanism (SHA-256 self-hash + staleness loop vs. Blob self-download + localStorage edition counter) and in argument (authentication-as-tautology vs. scarcity-as-fiction), but they share a Duchampian/Benjamin self-referential mode that has become a dominant mode in the 2026 entries; cumulative proximity to The Original and to several other self-referential 2026 pieces should be watched. The visible 'infrathin' note slightly explains a joke that was already legible from the console attesting — restraint could be tightened by removing the inline note and leaving only the console.
revision_suggestion: Drop the on-page infrathin note so the staleness gap is attested only in the console (the surface stays an innocent certificate, the depth lives in devtools) — this deepens the double-coding and trusts the mechanism more.
